ideas.hypothesis: Under the adaptive market hypothesis, measured weak-form efficiency should rise after structural shocks that change trader populations or costs (e.g., stamp duty changes) and fall during boom-bust transitions, so rolling-window efficiency scores will show regime-dependent swings that are predictable from volatility regime and policy events rather than a constant level.

ideas.test: Compute rolling 250-day variance ratio and MF-DFA efficiency indices for 4-6 Asian equity indices (daily data, 2000-2019); regress the efficiency index on a volatility-regime indicator (Markov-switching) and dummies for transaction tax changes, testing for significant shifts.
ideas.disconfirming: Efficiency indices are statistically flat over time, or show no change around regime shifts and transaction-tax events.

ideas.hypothesis: CAPM beta explains expected stock returns better in emerging markets once a time-varying market risk premium (proxied by dividend-growth-adjusted forecasts) is used instead of a constant premium, so the failure of unconditional Fama-MacBeth tests is partly due to ignoring premium variation.

ideas.disconfirming: Conditional-premium betas show no more significant pricing than unconditional betas, or size/value factors remain equally needed.
